title: Regular slicing through a closed Cohen–Macaulay fibre point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism] locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $s\in S$ and let $x$ be a closed point of the scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-weil-closed-points, def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Suppose the local ring $R=\mathcal O_{X_s,x}$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $\operatorname{depth}R=\dim R$ [def-weil-pbc-depth, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. There exist a scheme $Z$, an immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], and a point $z\in Z_s$ with $i(z)=x$, such that the composite $f\circ i:Z\to S$ is flat and locally of finite presentation, is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite], and $|Z_s|=\{z\}$. The immersion is regular: every point of $Z$ has an open neighbourhood $Z'\subseteq Z$ such that $i|_{Z'}$ factors as a closed immersion $Z'\to U$ followed by the inclusion of an affine open subscheme $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-open-immersion], with $Z'\cong\operatorname{Spec}(A/I)$ over $U$ and the ideal $I\subseteq A$ generated by a finite regular sequence $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in $A$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The case $r=0$, where $i|_{Z'}$ is an open immersion, is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0570 (lemma-slice-CM), specialized to a globally flat morphism, retaining regularity of the immersion.

proof.text: For each $d\in\mathbf N$ prove the following uniform assertion $P(d)$: every flat locally finitely presented $g:Y\to S$ and closed $y\in Y_s$ with Noetherian local ring $A=\mathcal O_{Y_s,y}$, $\dim A=d$ and $\operatorname{depth}A\ge d$, admit a regular immersion $i:Z\to Y$ and a point $z\in Z_s$ mapping to $y$, with singleton fibre $|Z_s|=\{z\}$ and $g\circ i$ flat, locally of finite presentation and locally quasi-finite. Use strong induction on $d$, uniformly in $Y,S,g,s,y$. The Noetherian-local dimension theorem makes $\dim R$ a finite nonnegative integer, so the item follows from $P(\dim R)$ using its depth equality. Using the depth inequality in the induction assertion permits the exact output of the hypersurface dimension-drop lemma.

source.place: Tag 0570 (lemma-slice-CM), induction; parameterized by local-ring dimension.

proof.text: For $d=0$, apply the zero-dimensional closed-fibre open-slice lemma to $g,s,y$. It gives an open immersion $V\to Y$ with singleton fibre and the required flatness, local finite presentation and local quasi-finiteness. An open immersion satisfies the stated regularity condition: choose an affine open of $Y$ inside its open image around each point, and use the empty sequence, with ideal $0$. The corresponding ring is nonzero because that affine open contains the point. Thus $P(0)$ holds.

For $d>0$, apply the CM fibre hypersurface dimension-drop lemma to $g,s,y,A$. Its depth hypothesis is exactly $\operatorname{depth}A\ge d$. Obtain $U=\operatorname{Spec}B\subseteq Y$, $a\in B$, $D=\operatorname{Spec}(B/(a))$ and a closed point $y_D\in D_s$ above $y$. Write $h$ for the germ of $a$ at $y$. The lemma supplies a nonzerodivisor $\bar h$ in the maximal ideal of $A$, flatness and local finite presentation of $D\to S$, and Noetherianity, dimension $d-1$ and depth at least $d-1$ for the actual local ring $\mathcal O_{D_s,y_D}$. It does not assert regularity of $D\to U$; establish that next.

Apply the prescribed-germ flat affine chart lemma to $g|_U$ at $y$ and $h$. Obtain affine charts $W=\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq U$, $V=\operatorname{Spec}H\subseteq S$ through the two points, with $H\to C$ flat and finitely presented, and a section $b\in C$ with germ $h$. The two sections $b$ and $a|_W$ have equal germs, so they agree on an open neighbourhood of $y$ by the definition of a sheaf stalk. Choose a principal neighbourhood in it using the basic-open basis. Rename the resulting affine ring $C$ and section $b$; now $b=a|_W$. Localization preserves flatness and finite presentation: the former follows from flat localization and composition, while a finite presentation for $C$ acquires just one variable and the relation $tq-1$ upon inverting $q$. The retained ring map is therefore flat and finitely presented.

source.place: Tag 056Y (lemma-slice-given-element), flat affine chart and prescribed section; Tag 0570, regularity of the cut.

proof.text: Identify the fibre of this affine chart with $\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(s)\otimes_H C)$ by the affine fibre-product lemma, and its local ring at the point over $y$ with $A$ by the affine-stalk lemma and the open-immersion stalk identification. The image of $b$ is $\bar h$, hence the singleton list $(b)$ is regular there: multiplication is injective and the quotient is nonzero since $\bar h$ lies in the maximal ideal. Apply the specified fibre regular-sequence neighbourhood lemma to $H\to C$ and this singleton. It supplies $q\notin Q$ such that $b$ is regular in $C_q$. Replace $D$ by its intersection with $\operatorname{Spec}C_q$. It is now cut out in this affine open of $Y$ by the regular singleton $b$, so its immersion $k:D\to Y$ is regular. This replacement is an open neighbourhood of $y_D$ in the previous $D$: flatness persists since the stalk maps are unchanged, and local finite presentation persists by restricting affine charts and adjoining a localization variable as in step 4. The fibre local ring and closedness of $y_D$ are unchanged. Therefore all dimension and depth conclusions of step 3 still hold.

source.place: Tag 0570 (lemma-slice-CM), regularity of the Cartier cut; specified-list regularity lifting from Tag 063W (lemma-fibre-quasi-regular).

proof.text: Since $0\le d-1<d$, apply $P(d-1)$ to $D\to S$ and $y_D$, with the Noetherian local ring and depth bound retained above. Obtain a regular immersion $j:Z\to D$ and $z\in Z_s$ with $j_s(z)=y_D$, singleton fibre and all required properties for $Z\to S$. Put $i=k\circ j$. The general composition theorem for regular immersions makes $i$ regular. Its hypotheses hold by step 5 and induction; no Noetherianity of $S,Y$ or $D$ is used. The composite to $S$ is exactly the one furnished by induction, so it remains flat, locally finitely presented and locally quasi-finite.

The universal property of the scheme-theoretic fibre identifies $i_s$ with $k_s\circ j_s$: both have the same projection to $Y$ and the same projection to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(s)$. Consequently $i_s(z)=k_s(y_D)=y$. The scheme $Z_s$ and its singleton assertion are those already provided by induction, since its structure morphism has not changed. This completes $P(d)$ and the induction. Here evaluating $i$ on a fibre point means applying $i$ to its image under the fibre projection.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0570 (lemma-slice-CM), dimension induction; regularity retained by specified-list lifting (Tag 063W) and composition (Tag 067Q).

For d>0, every hypothesis of the dimension-drop node is checked. Steps 4-5 recover regularity of the cut: prescribed-germ flat chart, germ agreement on a basic open, flat/fp localization, then the 063W specified-list lifting (lem-pur-fiber-regular-sequence-neighbourhood) applied to (b) with b̄=h̄ a nonzerodivisor in n, on D∩Spec C_q. Composition comes from the new node; fibre points follow from the universal property. The new node is a true statement-only node (067Q(1) via joining regular sequences; edge cases r=0, open immersions and non-Noetherian schemes checked). It is not a clause of the item and not a duplicate: lem-per-regular-lci-geometric-calculus is Noetherian and closed-only, and the project's IsRegularImmersion.comp needs a globally closed immersion with fixed codimension. Batch-5 flags: the closures of lem-trf-cm-fibre-hypersurface-dimension-drop (17 nodes), lem-trf-flat-affine-chart-prescribed-germ (135) and lem-trf-zero-dimensional-closed-fibre-open-slice (60) contain no other trf/pd node, no assumption leaf and no trace-transport node.
